title: The Great Banquet and the Cost of Discipleship

questions.question: One Sabbath, when Jesus went to dine at the house of a ruler of the Pharisees, who was in front of Him suffering from an illness?
options: A man who had dropsy
A man covered with advanced leprosy
A young boy who was blind from birth
A Roman soldier paralyzed in his legs
questions.explanation: Luke 14:2 (ESV): "And behold, there was a man before him who had dropsy."

questions.question: When Jesus asked the lawyers and Pharisees if it was lawful to heal on the Sabbath, how did they respond?
options: But they kept silent
They yelled "No, it is unlawful!"
They told him to heal him outside the house
They quoted Moses extensively in debate
questions.explanation: Luke 14:3-4 (ESV): "And Jesus responded to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, 'Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath, or not?' But they kept silent."

questions.question: What did Jesus say to justify healing the man with dropsy on the Sabbath?
options: "Which of you, having a son or an ox that has fallen into a well on a Sabbath day, will not immediately pull him out?"
"Is it not lawful to pluck grain when you are hungry?"
"Do you not tie your boats tightly to the docks on the Sabbath?"
"Did David not eat the showbread in the temple?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Which of you, having a son or an ox that has fallen into a well on a Sabbath day, will not immediately pull him out?"
questions.explanation: Luke 14:5 (ESV): "And he said to them, 'Which of you, having a son or an ox that has fallen into a well on a Sabbath day, will not immediately pull him out?'"

questions.question: When invited to a wedding feast, why should you not sit down in a place of honor?
options: Lest someone more distinguished than you be invited, and you are asked to move to the lowest place with shame
Because it is reserved for the religious scribes
Because the host desires it left empty for angels
Because you might be asked to pay extra for the food
questions.correctAnswer: Lest someone more distinguished than you be invited, and you are asked to move to the lowest place with shame
questions.explanation: Luke 14:8-9 (ESV): "do not sit down in a place of honor, lest someone more distinguished than you be invited... and you begin with shame to take the lowest place."

questions.question: "For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be..."?
options: Exalted
Honored highly
Lifted quickly
Saved entirely
questions.explanation: Luke 14:11 (ESV): "For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted."

questions.question: When you give a dinner or banquet, who did Jesus say you should invite, because they cannot repay you?
options: The poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind
The priests, the Levites, the beggars
Your brothers, your relatives, your rich neighbors
The tax collectors and the Gentile centurions
questions.correctAnswer: The poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind
questions.explanation: Luke 14:13 (ESV): "But when you give a feast, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind,"

questions.question: If you invite those who cannot repay you, when will you be repaid?
options: At the resurrection of the just
In the next Jubilee year
When the temple is rebuilt
At your deathbed
questions.correctAnswer: At the resurrection of the just
questions.explanation: Luke 14:14 (ESV): "and you will be blessed, because they cannot repay you. For you will be repaid at the resurrection of the just."

questions.question: In the Parable of the Great Banquet, a man gave a great banquet and sent his servant to say "Come, for everything is now ready." What was the first excuse given by an invited guest?
options: "I have bought a field, and I must go out and see it. Please have me excused."
"I cannot come, my mother is ill."
"I have to pay taxes to Caesar today."
"My workers have abandoned my harvest."
questions.correctAnswer: "I have bought a field, and I must go out and see it. Please have me excused."
questions.explanation: Luke 14:18 (ESV): "The first said to him, 'I have bought a field, and I must go out and see it. Please have me excused.'"

questions.question: What was the second excuse given in the parable?
options: "I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to examine them. Please have me excused."
"I have a great chest of gold to bury out in the desert."
"I am finishing a new roof on my house."
"I have injured my leg and cannot walk that far."
questions.correctAnswer: "I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to examine them. Please have me excused."
questions.explanation: Luke 14:19 (ESV): "And another said, 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to examine them. Please have me excused.'"

questions.question: What was the third excuse given in the parable?
options: "I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come."
"I just bought a new vineyard and must prune it."
"I am studying the scrolls with a famous rabbi."
"I am attending a funeral of a dear friend."
questions.correctAnswer: "I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come."
questions.explanation: Luke 14:20 (ESV): "And another said, 'I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.'"

questions.question: When the master became angry, where did he command the servant to go quickly and bring people in from?
options: The streets and lanes of the city
The highest hills outside Samaria
The Roman governor's palace
The synagogues scattered across Judea
questions.correctAnswer: The streets and lanes of the city
questions.explanation: Luke 14:21 (ESV): "Then the master of the house became angry and said to his servant, 'Go out quickly to the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor and crippled and blind and lame.'"

questions.question: When there was still room, what did the master tell the servant to do?
options: "Go out to the highways and hedges and compel people to come in, that my house may be filled."
"Invite the animals from the forest to eat the crumbs."
"Tear down the walls so the whole city can enter."
"Close the doors, the feast is now starting."
questions.correctAnswer: "Go out to the highways and hedges and compel people to come in, that my house may be filled."
questions.explanation: Luke 14:23 (ESV): "And the master said to the servant, 'Go out to the highways and hedges and compel people to come in, that my house may be filled.'"

questions.question: Jesus said to the great crowds: "If anyone comes to me and does not ___ his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, yes, and even his own life, he cannot be my disciple." What word completes the statement?
options: hate
ignore
forsake entirely
leave behind
questions.explanation: Luke 14:26 (ESV): "If anyone comes to me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children... he cannot be my disciple." (Used rhetorically to signify prioritizing God above all else).

questions.question: Jesus gave two examples of considering the cost of discipleship. One is a king going to war; what is the other?
options: A man desiring to build a tower who first sits down and counts the cost to see if he has enough to complete it
A merchant buying a vast fleet of ships to cross the sea
A farmer planting a very large vineyard in rocky soil
A shepherd counting his sheep in the dark valley
questions.correctAnswer: A man desiring to build a tower who first sits down and counts the cost to see if he has enough to complete it
questions.explanation: Luke 14:28 (ESV): "For which of you, desiring to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost, whether he has enough to complete it?"

questions.question: Why does Jesus mention salt losing its taste at the end of Chapter 14?
options: If salt has lost its taste, how shall its saltiness be restored? It is of no use either for the soil or for the manure pile
It proves the world is wicked and ruins everything pure
It shows the disciples must keep traveling continuously
It means the ocean will dry up in the last days
questions.correctAnswer: If salt has lost its taste, how shall its saltiness be restored? It is of no use either for the soil or for the manure pile
questions.explanation: Luke 14:34-35 (ESV): "Salt is good, but if salt has lost its taste, how shall its saltiness be restored? It is of no use either for the soil or for the manure pile. It is thrown away."

key_verse_text: "So therefore, any one of you who does not renounce all that he has cannot be my disciple."
